dedupe_keys.name: africa broadband outlook 2024 africa analysis position paper for the african telecommunications union

description: The Africa Broadband Outlook 2024 is a position paper analysing the development of fixed broadband infrastructure, especially fibre-optic networks, across Africa and the adoption of fixed broadband services. It segments African countries into three groups, Leading Markets, Developing Markets and Initial Markets, discusses how policy and regulatory frameworks differ by stage, proposes targets for fixed broadband connectivity for different user types by 2030 and the actions needed, reviews pan-African policies and strategies, and draws lessons from countries elsewhere that have built out fixed broadband. It notes that long-haul and metro segments have largely been upgraded while last-mile access still needs considerable investment, and that broadband penetration in Africa remains among the lowest globally. Producer: Africa Analysis (South Africa), publication date November 2024, hosted by the ATU. Coverage: the African continent, by country group. Access: a free 66-page PDF (a draft-final version). Licence and cost: free; no licence found in the pages read. Caveats: a policy paper with qualitative segmentation and target recommendations, with data tables that must be checked against the PDF, and the file name indicates a draft-final version. Simulation uses: the segmentation and 2030 targets provide scenario assumptions for broadband roll-out and capacity-planning models in Africa. Related record: the African IXP Association directory (data-african-ixp-association-directory).
